summary: Implement and verify the restricted PTX 9.4 scalar message-passing foundation in pinned Lean 4.33.0: publication, successful execution, relaxed counterexample, arena safety, reusable local/relational semantics, source correspondence and study guide. Independent semantic and proof reviews completed without blocking findings; proof validity is distinct from source fidelity.

examined.reason: Implemented the bounded responsibility: generated operational events, source-linked relational validity, publication, complete successful and relaxed witnesses, aligned arena safety, independent semantic/proof reviews, and reproducible dependency checks. Explicit restrictions exclude unsupported PTX features and hardware progress.

Added the scalar child and repaired implementation links to checked study/representation. Marked the broad responsibility partial: this fragment supplies the first operational/axiomatic semantics, while full ISA and computing-model coverage remain absent.

Linked the clause-by-clause source ledger and reproducible source/build/dependency checks. Recorded source-reviewed normalization separately from Lean validity. Model-generation infrastructure, external hardware validation, and broader coverage remain unimplemented.
Updated realization to partial for the first completed restricted fragment; retained full PTX/TorchLean/numerical/example responsibilities and their existing summary unchanged.
No differentiation, TorchLean automatic backward, or PTX backward implementation was added. The separation between correctness, execution existence, and termination is preserved.
The abstract single-GPU arena has no allocator, launch, lifetime, multi-kernel, or runtime execution model. Existing orchestration contracts remain unimplemented.
No tensor, numerical, TorchLean, or kernel-composition interface was introduced. The memory fragment is a future foundational dependency, not fulfillment of these contracts.
The only bitvector values are scalar u32 payloads with no arithmetic or floating point. No precision policy, real-valued approximation, or PyTorch correspondence is changed.
The foundations litmus study exercises PTX memory semantics, not end-to-end network verification. The Examples responsibility retains its existing network-level contract.
No Gemma architecture, implementation, cache, backward, loss, or numerical policy was changed.

results.method: scripts/check.sh; stratic validate; local documentation link/HTML-fragment validation; git diff --check; independent semantic and proof reviews
results.environment: Lean 4.33.0 (d8b18978322de05a8f3dba51ef03cf5461676c17), bundled libraries only; Python 3 standard library; Stratic 0.1.0; pinned PTX ISA 9.4 HTML; Linux x86_64; no GPU execution or paid external model calls
results.evidence: Snapshot unchanged before/after checks. Lean build and 31 theorem dependency reports pass; only standard propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice occur. Source scan rejects proof placeholders/custom axioms/native_decide. PTX SHA-256 0aa31c15735a30b5d7c0fa1fe02570dcd37fe80800afca74bcc96c9132b81fed, 3928316 bytes, and 23 exact manifest anchors verified. All 50 local documentation links/fragments resolve; Stratic structure and passage links validate; whitespace checks pass. A clean rebuild also passed for the same Lean sources. Independent semantic review found no blocker after clarifying target eligibility versus checked arena safety and paper-only remaining outcome rows. Independent proof review rebuilt the library and inspected 16 declarations, confirming generated event provenance, actual final-register projection, arbitrary source/coherence publication, complete admitted witnesses, and no missing-proof/custom-axiom dependencies. Whole-word/initialization normalization remains a reviewed source argument rather than a general byte-model equivalence theorem; hardware progress and full PTX coverage are not claimed.
